extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: The Natural Questions corpus is a question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. Each question is paired with a Wikipedia page and annotated with a long answer, a short answer, or marked as null if no answer is present.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski; Jennimaria Palomaki; Olivia Redfield; Michael Collins; Ankur Parikh; Chris Alberti; Danielle Epstein; Illia Polosukhin; Jacob Devlin; Kenton Lee; Kristina Toutanova; Llion Jones; Matthew Kelcey; Ming-Wei Chang; Andrew M. Dai; Jakob Uszkoreit; Quoc Le; Slav Petrov
extraction.citeAs: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov. Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 7, pp. 453-466, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were sampled from real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, filtered using heuristics, and retained if a Wikipedia page appeared in the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data; Passive Data Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Queries were discarded during the sampling process if there was no Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated user queries from Google search engine logs and corresponding Wikipedia pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were presented with a question and a Wikipedia page and asked to identify a long answer (an HTML bounding box) and a short answer (a span, set of spans, or boolean). The task was divided into three stages: Question Identification, Long Answer Identification, and Short Answer Identification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was evaluated post hoc by four experts who independently annotated examples for correctness and then met to reach a consensus judgment. A subset of data also received 25-way annotations to analyze human variability.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training data; 5 for development and test data; 25 for a subset of 302 examples
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There may be biases in the choice of focusing on Wikipedia as the source of factual information.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are limited to queries of 8 words or more; excludes 'how to' questions; limited to Wikipedia as the domain; boolean answers are left to future work.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmark for research in open-domain question answering; end-to-end training data for the QA problem; driving research in natural language understanding; studying human performance in providing QA annotations; evaluating the performance of question answering systems.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries were filtered to keep those of 8 words or more that match specific heuristic patterns (e.g., starting with 'who', 'when', or 'where'). Questions were then filtered to keep only those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results. Finally, questions were deduplicated to ensure every question is unique under exact string match, and randomly split into train, development, and test sets.
